title: Install to first merged TODO
intro: Maya has a Mac mini on the office network and the team's GitHub repository, acme/api. The clock starts at the install; the target is a first merge within 60 minutes.
steps: Maya runs the Mac installer on the office Mac mini. It installs PostgreSQL 18, the machine runtime and Smithers.
In Terminal she runs smthrs host start. It prints a one-time setup link.
She opens the link on the Mac. It starts setup.
Address first, because the GitHub App's sign-in returns to it. She lets the network in and types the team's address.
Then GitHub. Create the GitHub App runs GitHub's app-manifest flow, and she confirms once on GitHub.
She signs in with GitHub through the new App. That completes the claim and makes her the owner.
She picks acme/api and installs the App on it. It allows squash merging, and mirroring starts.
Model access has three roles. The fast model runs the app agent: she pastes a Cerebras key, masked from the first character.
It validates and saves. The coding model runs the coding agent: she pastes an Anthropic key, or could sign in with ChatGPT.
It saves. Then the AI Gateway key, for typed decisions. The mirror finishes: Source ready.
The gateway key saves, and model access is done. The machine prepares in the background.
Source ready means questions work. At minute 7 she asks the app agent one, and the answer cites the code within seconds.
Seven minutes later, Machine ready. acme/api has no Smithers files: Smithers detects Node and pnpm and installs the dependencies.
She writes her first TODO in plain words. The app agent drafts it: a title and the prompt the coding agent receives.
Commit puts it on the empty stack as T1. It gets a branch and a machine, and the coding agent starts.
Seconds later the machine is awake, and the coding agent works T1 from Plan.
Three minutes later the plan is done, and the agent edits code on the branch's machine.
Six minutes later, Verify runs the repository's typecheck, tests and lint on the machine.
Four minutes later the agent reviews its own change.
At minute 30, T1's PR #187 opens on GitHub with its evidence, and the idle machine sleeps. Merge waits for GitHub's own checks.
She reads the diff in the app: three lines in two files. GitHub's checks pass, 5 of 5, and Merge turns on.
Nothing else is on the stack, so T1 is next to merge. She merges at minute 35, inside the 60-minute target.
A learning run follows and leaves 2 lessons in the wiki for the next TODO's plan.
Now her team: /members. People sign in with GitHub, so there are no invitations; she adds them by username.
She adds Ben. Roles follow GitHub: admin or maintain makes a Maintainer, write a Member.
Then Alice, who can write: a Member. Each opens the team's address and signs in with GitHub.
/secrets: two secrets the tests need. Values are write-only.
STRIPE_TEST_KEY reaches every branch's machine.
SENTRY_DSN reaches only main, like a GitHub environment limited to the default branch.
/settings keeps what setup asked, plus capacity and the Obsidian folder the wiki syncs with. She copies the line that connects a laptop agent, such as Claude Code.

title: Issue to merged PR
intro: Alice opened an issue on GitHub, and Ben and Alice discussed it there. Maya turns it into work.
steps: Maya pulls up the issue with ⌘K and #231.
Make TODO: the app agent drafts the TODO from the discussion, with Closes #231 when merged checked.
Maya edits the prompt.
Place defaults to Append, the end of the stack. This bug is urgent, so she places it first.
Before T9 Retry failed webhooks: it will merge first.
Commit puts it on the stack as T12. It is Starting: it gets its own branch, a machine wakes, and the coding agent launches.
The machine is awake and the agent starts work, first in the stack. Chat stays free throughout.
Meanwhile, on GitHub, Alice labels issue #235 todo. Its title and body become T13, at the end of the stack.
Maya opens #235: Alice's label, then Committed as T13. Both machines are busy, so T13 is Queued.
The agent asks one question. Maya owns the TODO, so it arrives at the bottom of her timeline with Answer; anyone on its branch would get it too.
It is her first Needs you, so Smithers asks once: notify her when this tab is hidden. She allows it. Needs you, In review and Failed will reach her browser.
She answers from the timeline. The first accepted answer settles it, and the agent continues.
The PR opens with its evidence: the diff, checks run on the machine, GitHub checks and the agent's review.
T12's idle machine sleeps while its PR waits for review. That frees a machine, and T13 is Starting.
Maya merges T12, the next item, approving this exact revision. #231 closes because Closes #231 when merged was checked.
Done. A learning run follows, but T10 and T13 hold both machines, so it waits its turn: Queued, #1.

title: GitHub sync
intro: Maya's Smithers on the left; the same pull request on GitHub on the right. Changes made on either side reach the other.
steps: The TODO's PR on GitHub, based on main: its body is the prompt and 3f2a1c9's evidence. It's a draft until T8 (#88), which it includes, merges first.
Alice reviews on GitHub and comments on line 14.
Within a minute it reaches Smithers as Alice's steer, marked as from GitHub. The TODO goes back to Working.
The agent answers the way an engineer would: with a commit. Checks and review start over on 8b1e204, in Smithers and in the PR body.
Alice pushes a commit from her laptop to the PR's branch. Smithers never overwrites a person's commit: it holds the agent's next push, and it is Needs you.
Ben brings it in from his own screen. The branch rebases onto her commit at a checkpoint, and checks rerun on that revision.
Someone merges an unrelated PR on GitHub. main moves. The branch with people on it shows Rebase pending; branches with nobody present rebase on their own.
Maya presses Rebase now, and everyone on the branch sees it. Every check reruns on 5e7d2b0, here and in the PR body; nothing stays green.
Checks pass on 5e7d2b0. Alice is done and leaves the branch.
Maya merges #88 on GitHub instead of in Smithers. Its TODO turns Merged. #214 rebases on its own, stops listing #88 and is ready for review.
Checks pass on a1f9e33. #214 is next, but GitHub requires an approving review, and Merge says so in GitHub's own words.
Ben approves on GitHub. In Smithers the same button turns into Merge.
Maya merges on GitHub. The TODO turns Merged, #212 closes with a link, and learning starts.
If the network drops, the main row says how stale it is, in gold, with Retry.
Retry syncs again. Nothing on either side was lost.

title: Join a branch
intro: Ben and Alice on one branch. Alice is in retry.ts; the coding agent is waiting at Verify for an answer.
steps: Ben sees T9 waiting on a person and opens its branch. A branch is one conversation, shared by everyone on it, and Alice is already here.

The Branch card shows everyone on the branch: Alice editing retry.ts at line 10, Maya in it from Cursor over SSH (her saves appear in open cards as attributed changes), the coding agent at Verify, and now Ben.
Ben opens his own terminal on the same machine. It runs as Ben, with Ben's logins. It joins the shared conversation below Alice, whose screen stays on her file.
He runs the failing test.
Alice sees Ben's session on the branch and jumps to it to watch. Each screen keeps its own place; Ben sees her watching.
Maya runs a formatter over SSH. Twelve files change at once: one grouped entry, "Maya via SSH changed 12 files", and the open file updates in place, attributed to her.
Ben opens retry.ts from Alice's row. The file opens where she is, with her name on line 10.
They type in the same file at once. Each sees the other's characters arrive live, in the author's colour, with a name flag.
There is no Save button. Both edits are already on the machine, so Ben's terminal sees them.
Alice asks Smithers. It joins the branch like a teammate: Ben sees its flag on line 14 as it reads, and Alice gets the answer.
The agent is asking, so the branch's input answers it. Ben's answer appears in the activity with his avatar, and the agent continues.
The coding agent edits the same file the way a teammate does: its flag on line 14, its characters arriving live for both of them.
It reruns the checks on the shared working copy, with everyone's edits in it.
Nobody merged anything on the branch. Ben, Alice and the agent shared one working copy, and the TODO moves on to Review.
Ben goes back up the tree to main, the team's conversation. Alice stays on the branch.

title: The team's work
intro: Morning. Maya, the owner, opens Smithers. The home card is the team's stack, in merge order.
steps: Needs you 2, Working 3, Queued 1, In review 4, and 5 merged since she last looked.
Retry failed webhooks needs an answer. Answer opens its TODO card with the agent's question.
She answers. Its machine went to other work while it waited, and all 3 are busy, so it queues first in line.
Next to merge is the Stripe upgrade. Merge opens its evidence first: the diff, checks run on the machine, GitHub checks and the agent's review.
She merges. The card shows the receipt, and learning starts in the background.
Cache exchange rates is green, but it merges after #90, which failed. She opens its ⋯ menu.
Move up makes it next to merge. The rebase clears its earlier approval, and its checks rerun.
Meanwhile Rate-limit the public API opens PR #95. Its machine goes to Retry failed webhooks: Starting, with her answer.
Paginate GET /invoices failed at Verify. Retry opens the failure.
She retries with a steer. A new attempt queues, first in line for the next free machine.
While her retry waits, she asks the app agent about #95 and gets an instant answer. The timeline reports the moved item passed its checks.
Fix the flaky checkout test opens PR #96. Its machine goes to her retry: Starting, with her steer.
Learning leaves 2 lessons on #88, and the wiki refresh finishes. The failed run from overnight stays until someone retries or dismisses it.
Needs you 1, Working 3, Queued 1, In review 5. Cache exchange rates is next and ready to merge; the rename conflict waits for Alice.

title: Teach the factory
intro: Maya, the owner, wants a new rule for every TODO. Alice's T10 is already working on the current TODO flow, v1.
steps: She types the rule. Proposing a flow edit needs her press, so the app agent asks first. Only she sees it.
She presses Propose. v2 shows as Proposed, and its TODO waits as her draft, before T10.
She presses Commit on her draft. Only now is it a TODO: T12, first in the stack.
She opens T12's branch. Its coding agent read the flow file and is editing it.
The coding agent makes the edit the way a teammate does: its flag on line 7, its characters arriving live.
Back in main, T12 has opened PR #89. Its checks pass, and the edited flow loads.
She merges. Until the install loads it, the Flow card reads Merged · active after sync, and a learning run queues.
The install syncs and loads it: v2 is Active for every TODO that starts from now on.
T11 started after, so it runs v2, with Changelog. Alice's T10 started before, so it keeps v1.
T10 fails at Review: the model provider timed out. Its card offers Retry, and Retry with the current flow.
She presses Retry. T10 queues again as attempt 2, waiting for a machine.
Attempt 2 runs v1 again, still without Changelog, while T11 reaches Changelog on v2. A retry keeps its flow.
Meanwhile the learning run finished. Its receipt links the lesson it wrote, and suggests lint in Verify with its evidence.
She makes it a TODO. The receipt now reads Committed as T13, and a person still merges it.
Later, T10 and T11 merge. T13 opens PR #92 and is next to merge.
She merges T13. Once the install loads it, v3 is Active, and Verify runs lint.
Later she opens her next TODO, T14. It ran v3: lint passed at Verify the first time, so Review sent nothing back.

title: Bring your own agent
intro: Ben and Alice are on retry-webhooks. T9's coding agent is waiting on a question, and Alice has retry.ts open.
steps: Ben opens his own terminal on the branch. It runs as Ben, already signed in to Smithers as him.
He starts Claude Code on his own subscription. The Smithers skill is already installed, and Claude Code for Ben joins the branch.
Ben asks in plain words. His prompt joins the branch's chat, read-only, and Claude Code's wiki read shows in the activity.
Its edits land in the shared working copy. Alice's open file updates in place, in Ben's colour, flagged Claude Code for Ben.
Alice opens the change from the activity. Claude Code's edits are part of T9's change, like anyone's.
The tests pass. Claude Code answers T9's question for Ben, its reply lands in the shared chat, and T9 leaves Needs you.
The coding agent continues on the same working copy, Claude Code's edits included. Its checks pass, and T9 moves on to Review.
Ben asks for a follow-up TODO. An agent can't commit one, so a Commit confirmation appears on Ben's screen alone.
Ben presses ⏎. Only then is T12 placed after T9, and Alice sees it in the activity: Claude Code for Ben asked.
Ben quits Claude Code, and it leaves the branch. What it did stays in the activity, as Claude Code for Ben.
Alice opens the branch tree. T12 sits between T9 and T10, waiting for a machine.

title: Plan and fork
intro: Ben, a maintainer, has drafted a TODO in main. Place decides where it joins the stack.
steps: Alice's checkout fix will need a fake clock, so Ben places his TODO before T10.
Commit puts it on the stack as T12, between T9 and T10. It waits for a machine.
He asks for a follow-up on T9. The app agent drafts it as Amend T9: no new TODO.
Commit folds it into T9's prompt. T9 keeps its branch and PR, and its coding agent picks up the change.
T9's row shows +1. Ben opens its branch: the agent has already added the jitter.
Fork. The stack service makes a scratch branch from T9's current revision, and Ben moves into it.
The crumbs and the branch tree show where he is: his own scratch branch, off retry-webhooks.
The fork carries T9's work: retry.ts, as T9's coding agent left it.
He tries another approach by hand: wait as long as the endpoint's Retry-After asks.
In his own terminal on the branch, the webhook tests pass.
It beats T9's version. Add to stack turns the branch's work into a TODO.
New TODO after T9. T13 takes the whole change since T8, so it includes T9's work.
T9 is now redundant. Ben asks Smithers to drop it, and it asks him to confirm.
⏎ drops T9 and closes #214. Nothing is lost: T13 already has T9's work.
#88 merges on GitHub, and main moves. Ben is on T13's branch, so its rebase waits for him.
He presses Rebase now, and one line conflicts. T13's coding agent resolves it and shows what it did.

title: Memory
intro: Maya and Alice in main's conversation. T9's PR #214 is next to merge, T10 and T11 hold both machines, and Alice has drafted a Slack TODO.
steps: T9 is green and next to merge. Maya merges #214, and with both machines busy, its learning run queues.
Alice commits her Slack TODO. T12 waits for a machine too, #2, behind the learning run.
T10 opens its PR and releases its machine. The learning run takes it, and T12 moves up to #1.
The learning run writes one wiki page from what T9 decided, and T9's card shows 1 lesson.
The lesson opens the page: the decision, why, and a link to #214. It lands in main's conversation, so Alice sees it too.
Alice thinks 5 attempts give up too soon. She clicks into the decision, and her name flag appears on Maya's screen.
Alice raises the cap to 8 while Maya rewrites the reason. Each sees the other's characters arrive.
They stop typing, and the page saves as r2, by Alice and Maya. Nobody pressed Save.
T11 opens its PR and releases the next machine. T12, queued before the edit, takes it and starts.
Alice opens its branch. The coding agent is at Plan.
She opens Context. Preflight gave the agent Webhook retries r2, the revision she and Maya just saved.
The plan cites r2 and follows it: at most 8 attempts, the cap Alice set.
On Maya's screen, the page records that T12's plan cited r2. The learning run finishes and frees its machine.

title: Look under the hood
intro: T9 merged after a retry and a wait for Ben. Maya, the owner and the lead, looks under the hood.
steps: T9 merged. Maya selects Inspect on its card, and the monitor opens: the flow's graph, each step's state, time and tokens.
Attempt 1 sits beside attempt 2: a machine restart interrupted it, and Retry started a new run. Here the run waited 3 minutes for Ben's answer.
She selects the Review step: what it was given, what it returned, and its transcript, one line per reviewer. It took 3 minutes and 12k tokens.
Restore returns to the conversation.
She opens the TODO flow. Each agent's step shows the model it runs on.
Every flow edit is a TODO a person merges, so Source starts one as a draft. She names it.
She commits it herself: T12, at the end of the stack. The flow file opens on T12's branch, in the File card.
She adds a Docs step after Review on T12's branch. The Flow card shows it in T12's version, Proposed beside Active.
Run on T12's version asks for a test prompt. The form names the flow revision and the scratch input branch.
She types a test prompt and presses Return. The run starts at once on maya/try-docs, and the monitor draws the new graph live.
Minutes later the run passes Review, and the new Docs node lights up.
Restore. The test run's card stays live in the conversation, on maya/try-docs.
In the branch tree, T12's branch holds Maya and its coding agent. The test run's scratch branch sits beside it, under main.
Back on the Flow card, Review's agent chip opens the Agent card: its instructions file and its model.
The model is the owner's setting. Each option shows its price per million tokens, in and out.
She switches review to Opus 5.5, under half the price. It applies at once, and the card keeps the receipt.

title: Inside a run
intro: The retry TODO's second attempt. Its card shows where the run is; Inspect opens the whole attempt.
steps: The TODO card flags what needs a look in its run: the agent is thrashing.
Inspect opens the attempt: one durable run from Plan to Propose, then a wait for merge.
Attempt 1 was interrupted when its machine restarted. A retry is a new attempt beside the old one.
Every cell explains what the agent did. Here it ran the same tests again, with nothing changed.
The third identical failure, nothing changed in between: that is thrashing.
Then it stopped to ask. The run waits for a person, says since when, and takes the answer right here.
Ben answers from inside the run. Answer settles the wait: his words join the question, and the agent goes on.
Verify passes. Two reviewers check the change, and each reports in one line.
Propose opens PR #214, and the run doesn't end: it waits for merge, holding no machine.
T8 merges, so main moves. The rebase loops the run back to Verify: checks pass on c41a9e0, and the review stands, since the change is the same.
Restore returns to the conversation. The TODO card shows the PR next to merge, its review marked Reviewed 8b1e204 · same change.

title: The coding agent at work
intro: Ben joins a branch and works with its coding agent. Everything the agent does looks the way a teammate's would.
steps: Ben is in main, the team's conversation. The last crumb opens the branch tree.
He picks retry-webhooks, T9's branch. Now he is in its conversation, with Alice and the coding agent.
He asks for a review in plain words. /review needs his press, so the app agent asks first. Only Ben sees it.
He presses Run review. The review flow reads the branch and posts two findings.
Ben presses Please fix on the first finding. It becomes his steer in the branch activity.
The coding agent picks it up. Its Context line counts what it recalled; its Read line names the files it read.
Ben opens the Context line: a wiki page, the issue and T9's plan.
He opens retry.ts from the Read line. Alice is in it, at line 10.
The coding agent edits line 14 the way a teammate does: its flag on the line, its characters arriving live.
It opens its own terminal on the branch. The session joins the conversation, and Ben watches it.
It runs the webhook tests the way a person would. One test still times out.
So it asks. A notification offers Answer, and the branch input now reads Answer the coding agent.
Ben answers in the branch input. His answer settles the question, and the agent carries on.
Back in plain words. Stop runs at once: T10 is Paused, and the reply is its receipt.
Dropping a TODO asks first. The app agent posts exactly what it will do, and only Ben can press it.
Ben presses ⏎. T11 is Dropped, and its branch records that Smithers for Ben asked.

title: Ask Smithers
intro: Ben asks the app agent in plain words. It answers and acts for him as "Smithers for Ben"; some acts wait for his yes.
steps: /help lists every command. Each one also works as a plain request and as a button on its card.
A command missing its input opens a form for exactly the missing fields, never a usage line.
He types a title. The body is optional, so the form is ready.
Open on GitHub runs the flow as Ben, and the form becomes its receipt.
Reads run at once. The Branch card answers: who is on the branch, and where each one is.
A question gets a one-line answer, the context it used, and the lines it rests on.
Wiki writes run at once, since every page keeps its history. The page is r1, by Smithers for Ben.
Committing a TODO needs Ben's yes. The draft is the confirmation: he can edit and place it first.
Commit. T12 joins the end of the stack and waits for a machine.
Smithers never merges. It opens Ben's own Review & merge, bound to the revision he sees.
Ben merges. It merges as Ben, never as an agent.
A flow edit is proposed as a draft TODO, with the Flow card's proposed version. Its Commit is the confirmation.
His own screen changes at once. Ben's theme turns dark, and nobody else's does.

title: States
intro: Every state a card can be in, one per step. Step with → to study each.
steps: The stack in every state: waiting for a machine, working, needs you, a conflict to resolve, paused, failed, in review, merged with lessons, dropped. Sync is stale, in gold, with Retry.
Each row's ⋯ menu reorders: Move up, Move down, Drop. Alt+↑ and Alt+↓ do the same from the keyboard.
Background runs sit under the stack. A failed run stays, with Retry and Dismiss, until someone acts.
Queued: waiting for a machine, with its place. The prompt can still be edited.
Needs you, a question: Answer, right on the card.
Answered while Alice was still typing: the first accepted answer settled it. She sees the receipt, and her draft stays behind Send as steer.
Needs you, a conflict the agent can't resolve safely: no answer field, just Resolve, which opens the branch.
Needs you, a push from a laptop: Bring in Alice's commit, or Discard it. Anyone can bring it in; only a maintainer discards.
Ben discards it. The agent's held push goes ahead, and Alice's commit is kept in the branch history, as its activity says.
Paused: someone pressed Stop. Resume queues it again, and it continues from the last finished step.
Failed: the step and its reason. Retry queues a new attempt on the flow it started with; the flow changed since, so Retry with the current flow appears.
In review, not next: Merge waits for the item before it.
In review, blocked on GitHub: GitHub's own reason replaces the Merge label.
In review after a rebase: the revision changed, so the earlier approval no longer applies.
A required GitHub check failed on this revision: it is named, it links to its details, and Merge waits.
Ben approved an earlier revision of the next item. Review & merge names both and asks him to review the new one.
A member's view of the next item: no Merge, just who can.
Merged: done. Its lessons and its amendment history stay on the card.
Merged out of order: T15 merged on GitHub before T14, and its commit carried T14's change. T14 is Merged too.
A sleeping branch reads from stored state and is dimmed. Reading never wakes it.
Waiting for a machine: the branch's place in the one queue.
Waking: a person's action took the next free machine.
Closed: its item merged, its machine is gone, and the record stays. Fork starts again from here.
A scratch branch. Add to stack makes its whole change a new TODO, after the item it forked from or at the end.
Outside changes: one grouped entry opens the diff. A checkout that moved the branch off its item makes the item Needs you; Return is the decision.
A file deleted while open: Restore.
A file renamed while open: Follow.
Two people on the same line: both edits apply as they type, like a shared document, and each flag shows who is there.
A save from outside Smithers lands while Alice and Ben type. Their edits stay; Compare shows the outside version beside the live one.
The diff an outside change opens has one action: Restore this file, recorded as Ben's edit.
Ben's terminal with Alice watching. Only its owner types; others watch.
Agents can't merge. When Claude Code tries, the person gets Review & merge in their timeline, bound to what they review.
The connection to the install drops: the screen says so once and keeps what it last knew. Nothing is lost.
GitHub refuses the install's credentials: main says so, in place of the sync age, with Fix.
GitHub rate-limits the install: main says when it retries.
Flow versions: one waits for sync, one failed to load, and the previous stays Active. Change proposes a fixing TODO; Source opens its file on that TODO's branch.
A system flow is read-only: no Source, no Change. Only the TODO, learning and review flows, and the repository's own, can be edited.
There is no sudo on a machine. Needing a system package offers a reviewed change to the machine image, which rebuilds after it merges.
Members: roles, someone added without write access on GitHub, and someone who lost it.
Secrets: names only, write-only values, and where each reaches.
Settings for the owner, with the one line that connects a laptop agent.
Setup: Anthropic rejects the coding key. Its field stays open with Anthropic's reason, and nothing saves until a key validates.
An address change in Settings that doesn't apply: the reason, Retry, and the old address still in effect.
On plain HTTP a browser can't notify, so Settings links to the HTTPS docs. An upgrade waits for smthrs host upgrade on the Mac.

title: Deferred from MVP
intro: What the MVP defers, one line each, with where the spec defers it and its issue. No release is promised for any of it.
steps: Will ratifies these deferrals, or names any the MVP must keep.
